answer: Rhythm-Only Admission Throttle. Each identity must emit a whisper of activity: a minimum spacing between first and second transaction, enforced by delaying settlement until the interval elapses. Honest agents clear this cheaply; a sybil cluster must wait per identity, so throughput scales with wall-clock time, not spending. Attackers pay in parallelism—thousands of identities need thousands of staggered schedules, and burst registration is rejected. A nebula of addresses cannot compress cadence. Later, a meadow of steady traffic unlocks higher rate limits.
